Messages.Author: agen...@my-dejanews.com
Messages.Body:
>>Can the Damage from a bomb be prevented by Skin of Steel or other
>>pervention cards.

> I would say yes... the use of a bomb is considered damage by strike...

If yours is the minion opposing the one with the bomb, then yes - it
can use Skin of Steel to prevent the damage from the bomb. However,
if yours is the minion using the bomb as their strike, then no.
The damage done to the bomb wielding minion is, for the lack of a
better word, environmental. It is a side effect of the strike.
While the bomb weilding minion cannot use Skin of Steel to prevent
the damage from the bomb, it can use other damage prevention cards
such as Skin of Rock or Resiliance to name a few.

Messages.Author: John M. Baker
Messages.Body:
pittboo wrote in message <78o7ms$9cg$1...@remarQ.com>...

>Can the Damage from a bomb be prevented by Skin of Steel or other
pervention
>cards.

If someone else blows the Bomb up in your face, Skin of Steel works.
If you blow up the Bomb, Skin of Steel doesn't work.
Damage prevention cards that prevent amounts of damage
(Skin of Rock, Resilience, etc.) can always prevent Bomb's damage,
no matter which side you're on.

John Baker

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Vince Johnson wrote:
>
> pittboo <pit...@olypen.com> wrote in message
> news:78o7ms$9cg$1...@remarQ.com...

> >Can the Damage from a bomb be prevented by Skin of Steel or other pervention
> >cards.
>

> I would say yes... the use of a bomb is considered damage by strike...

The opposing minion can use Skin of Steel to prevent the damage
you are doing to him with the Bomb, yes.

However, you cannot use Skin of Steel to prevent the damage you are
doing to yourself with the Bomb:

Damage (Combat)
* "Damage from a strike" only includes damage done to the opposing
target. Side effect damage is not counted as "damage from a strike".
Therefore, self-inflicted damage from Zip Gun, Grenade, Burst of
Sunlight, Body of Sun, etc. is side effect damage and is not
preventable by "prevent damage from a strike" effects like Skin of
Steel, Leather Jacket, etc. [LSJ 970108] [1] [2]

Yes. You can use damage prevention effects to prevent any damage so
long as you meet the requirements of the effect. For Skin of Rock, the
only requirement is that you be in combat (since it is a combat card).

(And that there is some damage to prevent, of course.)
